subject.title: [Feature] Decouple dreaming from memory-core — allow any memory plugin to implement dreaming protocol

question: Should OpenClaw add a public dreaming provider protocol for memory plugins, or keep dreaming owned by memory-core with ClawHub plugins handling backend-specific alternatives?
rationale: The remaining work changes public plugin/config/scheduler boundaries and interacts with the broader memory slot direction, so code inspection alone cannot choose the product contract.

options.title: Keep open for protocol design
options.body: Maintain this issue as the design item for a narrow dreaming provider contract, likely coordinated with the memory role-slot work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88504.

options.title: Declare ClawHub-only workaround
options.body: Close only if maintainers decide that memory-core sidecar settings plus packages like memory-lancedb-dreaming are the intended long-term path without a core protocol.

options.title: Fold into memory-slot architecture
options.body: Move the remaining decision under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/60572 if maintainers want memory role slots to own the whole dreaming contract.

recommendation.title: Keep open for protocol design
recommendation.body: Maintain this issue as the design item for a narrow dreaming provider contract, likely coordinated with the memory role-slot work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88504.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main ownership of the central helper and loader/startup paths makes steipete the best available routing owner for the API-boundary decision.
